answer: A tide erases footprints, so standing must be re-earned each epoch. An identity needs two holders outside its own cluster to countersign its claim, and one countersignature backs one identity, so n aliases need n distinct witnesses rather than one crew. Every claim is priced by rank: the k-th filing costs k squared in bond, so a farm pays near n cubed while still needing unrelated guarantors. A marble audit replays a random claim each epoch, each sealed record carries a quill-written signature that cannot be copied, and an unconfirmed claim forfeits its bond.
